relations.quote: Gaussian resampling is a technique that replaces a [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md) of arbitrary length by transforms whose axis lengths are powers of two.

relations.predicate: replaces the Fourier transforms needed for
relations.quote: Gaussian resampling replaces the Fourier transforms needed for a [radix-digit convolution](radix-digit-convolution.md) by transforms whose axis lengths are powers of two.

symbols.name: source length
symbols.meaning: The number of coordinates of a source vector.
symbols.quote: Here $s$ is the number of coordinates of a source vector, and $t$ is the number of coordinates of a target vector, with $s<t$ and $\gcd(s,t)=1$.

symbols.name: target length
symbols.meaning: The number of coordinates of a target vector.
symbols.quote: Here $s$ is the number of coordinates of a source vector, and $t$ is the number of coordinates of a target vector, with $s<t$ and $\gcd(s,t)=1$.

symbols.name: Gaussian width
symbols.meaning: The integer width parameter of the Gaussian weights.
symbols.quote: The integer $\alpha$ is the width parameter of the Gaussian weights.

symbols.name: source transform
symbols.meaning: The normalized Fourier transform of length s.
symbols.quote: $F_s$ and $F_t$ are the normalized Fourier transforms of length $s$ and $t$.

symbols.name: target transform
symbols.meaning: The normalized Fourier transform of length t.
symbols.quote: $F_s$ and $F_t$ are the normalized Fourier transforms of length $s$ and $t$.

symbols.name: source permutation
symbols.meaning: The coordinate permutation on vectors of length s, sending g to the vector whose j-th entry is g_{tj}.
symbols.quote: $P_s$ and $P_t$ are the coordinate permutations $(P_s g)_j=g_{tj}$ and $(P_t h)_m=h_{-sm}$ on vectors $g$ of length $s$ and $h$ of length $t$, where $j$ and $m$ are coordinate indices (the letter $j$ changes meaning here; it is not the input index of the transform above), and subscripts are taken modulo the length.

symbols.name: target permutation
symbols.meaning: The coordinate permutation on vectors of length t, sending h to the vector whose m-th entry is h_{-sm}.
symbols.quote: $P_s$ and $P_t$ are the coordinate permutations $(P_s g)_j=g_{tj}$ and $(P_t h)_m=h_{-sm}$ on vectors $g$ of length $s$ and $h$ of length $t$, where $j$ and $m$ are coordinate indices (the letter $j$ changes meaning here; it is not the input index of the transform above), and subscripts are taken modulo the length.

symbols.name: coordinate index
symbols.meaning: The index of a coordinate in the permutation formulas, here a different use from the input index of the transform.
symbols.quote: $P_s$ and $P_t$ are the coordinate permutations $(P_s g)_j=g_{tj}$ and $(P_t h)_m=h_{-sm}$ on vectors $g$ of length $s$ and $h$ of length $t$, where $j$ and $m$ are coordinate indices (the letter $j$ changes meaning here; it is not the input index of the transform above), and subscripts are taken modulo the length.

symbols.name: target coordinate index
symbols.meaning: The index of a coordinate of a target vector in the permutation P_t.
symbols.quote: $P_s$ and $P_t$ are the coordinate permutations $(P_s g)_j=g_{tj}$ and $(P_t h)_m=h_{-sm}$ on vectors $g$ of length $s$ and $h$ of length $t$, where $j$ and $m$ are coordinate indices (the letter $j$ changes meaning here; it is not the input index of the transform above), and subscripts are taken modulo the length.

symbols.name: identity map
symbols.meaning: The identity map, the map that leaves every vector unchanged.
symbols.quote: $I$ is the identity map, and $\|\cdot\|$ is the operator norm: the largest factor by which a linear map stretches a vector, measured in the maximum-modulus norm (the largest absolute value of a coordinate).

symbols.name: operator norm
symbols.meaning: The operator norm of a linear map, the largest factor by which it stretches a vector in the maximum-modulus norm.
symbols.quote: $I$ is the identity map, and $\|\cdot\|$ is the operator norm: the largest factor by which a linear map stretches a vector, measured in the maximum-modulus norm (the largest absolute value of a coordinate).

symbols.name: source-to-target map
symbols.meaning: One of two Gaussian-weighted maps from vectors of length s to vectors of length t.
symbols.quote: The identity rests on two Gaussian-weighted maps $S$ and $T$ from vectors of length $s$ to vectors of length $t$.

symbols.name: second Gaussian map
symbols.meaning: The second of two Gaussian-weighted maps from vectors of length s to vectors of length t.
symbols.quote: The identity rests on two Gaussian-weighted maps $S$ and $T$ from vectors of length $s$ to vectors of length $t$.

symbols.name: diagonal Gaussian map
symbols.meaning: The diagonal map on vectors of length s that multiplies each coordinate j by a Gaussian factor.
symbols.quote: $D$ is the diagonal map on vectors of length $s$ that multiplies coordinate $j$ by a Gaussian factor, and $C$ selects from a length-$t$ vector the coordinates at the indices nearest $tj/s$, for $0\le j<s$.

symbols.name: coordinate selection map
symbols.meaning: The map from vectors of length t to vectors of length s that selects the coordinates at the indices nearest tj/s.
symbols.quote: $D$ is the diagonal map on vectors of length $s$ that multiplies coordinate $j$ by a Gaussian factor, and $C$ selects from a length-$t$ vector the coordinates at the indices nearest $tj/s$, for $0\le j<s$.

symbols.name: near-identity map
symbols.meaning: The map CTD on vectors of length s, which is close to the identity map.

symbols.name: summation index
symbols.meaning: The index of the terms in the Neumann series for the inverse of N.
symbols.quote: Its inverse is the Neumann series $N^{-1}=\sum_{r\ge 0}(I-N)^r$, where $r$ is the summation index.

symbols.name: source contraction
symbols.meaning: The contraction S/2 applied to the source transform on the right of the identity.
symbols.quote: the maps $A=S/2$ and $B_0=2^{-(2\alpha^2-2)}DN^{-1}C/2$ are the two contractions of the identity; $B_0$ here is a map, not the radix $B$.

symbols.name: target contraction
symbols.meaning: The contraction 2^{-(2 alpha^2-2)} D N^{-1} C / 2 applied to the target transform on the left of the identity.
symbols.quote: the maps $A=S/2$ and $B_0=2^{-(2\alpha^2-2)}DN^{-1}C/2$ are the two contractions of the identity; $B_0$ here is a map, not the radix $B$.
